analysis.one_liner: Eternal Limited (formerly Zomato) runs online food delivery under the Zomato brand, quick-commerce grocery delivery under Blinkit, B2B restaurant supply under Hyperpure, and a dining-out/events platform under District.
analysis.whats_happening: Eternal reported Q2 FY27 (September 2026 quarter) results on October 21, 2026: consolidated net profit of ₹125 crore (up 92% YoY from ₹65 crore) on revenue of ₹24,138 crore (up 78% YoY). Blinkit swung to an EBITDA profit of ₹184 crore versus a ₹156 crore loss a year earlier, while Zomato's own order value grew 21.5% YoY. The stock closed at ₹343.65 on 2026-10-30, its highest close in the past 52 weeks and just 3% below the all-time high set on 2025-10-15.
analysis.plain_terms: Eternal has gone from a loss-making food-delivery app to a company posting a real, if still small, quarterly profit, with its grocery-delivery arm Blinkit now adding to profit instead of draining it. The tension: the market values the company at roughly ₹3 lakh crore while quarterly profit is only ₹125 crore, so almost none of that value is explained by today's earnings. It is a bet on where Blinkit's profitability and Zomato's order growth go from here, not on what the company earns right now. Also note that a large chunk of the eye-catching revenue growth is not real sales growth - it is Blinkit changing how it records revenue.
analysis.quarters: Zomato's core food-delivery net order value grew 21.5% YoY, the fifth straight quarter of accelerating growth - a genuine, volume-led improvement. Blinkit's net order value grew 79.3% YoY to roughly ₹20,940 crore and it added 308 stores (2,751 total), while its EBITDA turned positive (₹184 crore vs a ₹156 crore loss a year ago). However, management and multiple outlets flagged that Blinkit shifted from a commission-based model to an inventory-led model where it now books the full sale value of goods rather than just commission - this is why consolidated revenue jumped 78-94% YoY and why that revenue figure is not strictly comparable to prior-year quarters. The cleaner read is PAT (₹125 crore vs ₹65 crore) and company-wide EBITDA (₹752 crore vs ₹239 crore), both of which sit below that distortion, though even these are off a very small base. CFO Akshant Goyal said quick-commerce competition has intensified to 5-7 players but is now 'more predictable,' and that the company would rather invest further in growth than optimise near-term margins.
analysis.performance_read: No splits or demergers apply here (has_corporate_action is false), so the raw price series can be read at face value. Returns are strong but uneven: 3-year return of 227% and 5-year return of 159% since its July 2021 listing both crushed the Nifty (21% and 29% respectively) and the listed peer Swiggy, which is down over 57-61% on the same horizons. But the 1-year return is only 4.34%, meaning the stock went through a sharp mid-period drawdown (52-week low of ₹215.68) before recovering to today's near-peak level - the multi-year outperformance masks a genuinely volatile middle stretch.
analysis.valuation_read: Expensive on every current-earnings basis, and the 'why' matters: trailing P/E is reported anywhere from roughly 480x to 700x depending on the data source, which is a sign the ratio is close to meaningless at this earnings base - a tiny PAT swing moves it wildly (classic tiny-base distortion), not a verified single figure. More stable anchors - P/B of 6.8x and ROE of just 0.33% - show the market is paying a rich premium to book value for a business that currently converts almost none of that equity into profit. Whether that is 'cheap' depends entirely on whether Blinkit's newly positive EBITDA compounds toward its stated 5,000-store FY28 target; on today's actual earnings, it is not cheap by any conventional measure.
analysis.growth_read: Mixed and worth separating by segment. Zomato's food-delivery growth (21.5% NOV YoY, accelerating for five quarters) is volume-led and comparable quarter to quarter. Blinkit's growth is harder to read cleanly: order volumes and store count are genuinely scaling (2,751 stores, +308 in the quarter), but a large part of its reported revenue jump comes from the accounting switch to gross/inventory-led revenue recognition rather than organic sales growth. The profit improvement at Blinkit (EBITDA loss to EBITDA profit) does look margin-led at the unit-economics level, layered on top of real volume growth - but the headline consolidated revenue growth rate should not be taken at face value.
analysis.health_read: Total debt roughly doubled over FY26 to about ₹4,686 crore from ₹2,045 crore, plausibly tied to Blinkit's expanding dark-store lease liabilities and inventory financing as it scales the first-party model - this is worth tracking as store count grows toward 5,000. Whether operating profit is converting cleanly into operating cash flow is not verified here - check on Screener. Given the company has historically held substantial cash/investment balances from its IPO and follow-on raises (not independently verified here), the more relevant risk right now looks like business risk - intense, multi-player quick-commerce competition and thin consolidated margins - rather than balance-sheet distress, but this should be confirmed against the latest cash position.
analysis.ownership_read: Eternal has 0% promoter shareholding - founder Deepinder Goyal does not hold promoter classification, so there is no promoter pledging to track, structurally. Early strategic backer Antfin (Alibaba-linked) fully exited in August 2025, selling its remaining stake via block deal for about ₹5,370 crore. Info Edge (founded by Sanjeev Bikhchandani), however, is still on the register and a notable holder at roughly 12.4% as of September 2026 - its original investment of about ₹86 crore is now worth an estimated ₹32,000 crore, one of the best-known early bets in Indian internet investing. The rest of the register is institutionally dominated (FIIs, mutual funds and other DIIs), with public/retail holding a relatively small single-digit share.
strengths: Blinkit swung from an EBITDA loss of ₹156 crore to an EBITDA profit of ₹184 crore in a single year
Zomato's core food-delivery order value grew 21.5% YoY, its fifth consecutive quarter of accelerating growth
Consolidated PAT rose to ₹125 crore from ₹65 crore even while the company kept funding store expansion (2,751 Blinkit stores, +308 added this quarter)
3-year shareholder return of 227% has far outpaced the Nifty (21%) and the listed quick-commerce peer Swiggy (-61%)
watchpoints: The 78-94% headline revenue growth is largely an accounting artifact from Blinkit's shift to gross/inventory-led revenue recognition - not like-for-like organic growth
Reported P/E ranges from roughly 480x to 700x across data providers, reflecting a near-zero earnings base rather than any genuine 'cheapness' signal; ROE is just 0.33%
Total debt roughly doubled over FY26 to an estimated ₹4,686 crore - worth watching as the inventory-led, store-heavy model scales
Management itself flagged 'significantly increased competitive intensity' with 5-7 quick-commerce players, and says it will prioritise growth spending over near-term margin optimisation
analysis.one_thing: Whether Blinkit's newly positive EBITDA (₹184 crore this quarter) holds and compounds over the next few quarters as store count scales toward the stated 5,000-store FY28 target - that trajectory, not today's P/E, is what the current roughly ₹3 lakh crore valuation is actually pricing.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 PAT (₹125 crore) and revenue (₹24,138 crore) figures were cross-checked across Medianama, Entrackr, Yourstory and CIOL and are consistent. P/E ratio was inconsistent across trackers (479x, 598x, 703x cited by different sites) because trailing EPS is tiny - treat all as indicative, not verified. Current ROCE and operating-cash-flow conversion for FY26 are not independently verified - check on Screener. Total debt figure sourced from companiesmarketcap.com and not cross-checked against the audited balance sheet. Shareholding percentages (FII/DII/MF/public) are taken from a single tracker and do not cleanly sum without overlap, so treat the institutional split as directional only; the 0% promoter holding and Info Edge's ~12.4% stake were corroborated separately.
